newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China distillery plans IPO of 100 mln A shares.
newsitem.headline: China distillery plans IPO of 100 mln A shares.

text.p: Hunan Jiugui Distillery Co Ltd plans to launch an initial public offering of 100 million A shares and list them in Shenzhen in the first half of 1997, a company official said on Monday.

The offer, which needs approval from the China Securities Regulatory Commission, has been tentatively priced at between seven and eight yuan per share, the official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.

Jiugui (which means drunkard in Chinese) plans to use the proceeds to expand output of rice wines, the official said, adding the firm is likely to name the Beijing Securities Co Ltd as the chief underwriter.
The official said Jiugui, which has 150 million outstanding shares, estimated net profit of about 130 million yuan for 1996, against 70 million yuan in 1995 and 50 million yuan in 1994.
He said the company's earnings surged on increasingly robust demand, which allowed the firm to raise sales prices.
Based in Jishou city in central Hunan province, Jiugui sells most of its products domestically, he said.
